# **CardioGoodFit Data**

-   The market research team at AdRight is assigned the task to identify the profile of the typical customer for each treadmill product offered by CardioGood Fitness.

-   The market research team decides to investigate whether there are differences across the product lines with respect to customer characteristics.

-   The team decides to collect data on individuals who purchased a treadmill at a CardioGoodFitness retail store during the prior three months.

-   The data are stored in the CardioGoodFitness.csv file

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# **Know your Data Variables**

1.  product purchased, TM195, TM498, or TM798
2.  gender;
3.  age, in years;
4.  education, in years;
5.  relationship status, single or partnered;
6.  annual household income ;
7.  average number of times the customer plans to use the treadmill each week;
8.  average number of miles the customer expects to walk/run each week;
9.  self-rated fitness on an 1-to-5 scale, where 1 is poor shape and 5 is excellent shape

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Dplyr package

dplyr enables you manipulate data through:

-   Row manipulations

-   Column manipulation

-   Combining/Joining table or data frame

-   Loading the package

```{r}
#install.packages('tidyverse')
    library(dplyr)
    library(quarto)
    library(rmarkdown)
    ## Load data
    data("starwars")
    ##view
    head(starwars)
    str(starwars)
```

# The %\>% or \|\> operator

-   %\>% is a special operator in R found in the magrittr and dplyr packages.

-   %\>% lets you pass objects to functions elegantly,

-   make your code more readable.

```{r}
# strawars data
    df1<-starwars |> select(hair_color, skin_color, mass, height)
    head(df1)
```
    
    
# Row Manipulation

-   This uses the following verbs **filter, slice, arrange and distinct**

    ```{r}
    
    # Filter rows on one condition (e.g., eye color) 
    df_eye <- starwars %>% 
    filter(eye_color == "blue")

    # Filter on two OR more conditions 
    eye.hgt <-starwars %>% 
    filter(eye_color == "blue" | height > 105)
    # Filter on two AND more conditions  
    eye.mass <- starwars %>% 
    filter(eye_color == "blue"& mass <= 50)
    # Filter in another set of values  
    eye.bb <-starwars %>% 
    filter(eye_color %in% c( "blue", "brown"))

    # Filter rows based on row index  
    starwars %>% 
    slice(1:3)
    ```

# **Sort rows in Order**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: true 
# Sort rows by values in a column in ascending order 
df_ord <- starwars %>% 
arrange(mass)

# Sort rows by values in a column in descending order 

df_ord_dsc <-starwars %>% 
arrange(desc(mass))

# Remove duplicate rows in all the dataset 

df_distint <-starwars %>% 
distinct()
```    
 
# Column Manipulation

-   **select**: select one or more columns with select()

    ```{r}
    #| echo: true
    #| eval: true 
    df2<-starwars |> select(hair_color, eye_color, 
                    skin_color, mass, height, birth_year)

    # Select columns based on start characters 
    df_hh <-starwars %>% select(starts_with("h"))

    # Select columns based on end characters 
    df_color <-starwars %>% select(ends_with("color"))

    # Rename a column using rename() 
    df_age <- df2 %>% rename(Age.yrs =birth_year)

    ```

# Creating new Columns

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: true
 
#create a bmi column : bmi = mass/height
df_bmi <- df2 %>% mutate(BMI = mass/(height/100)^2)

#Create a skin eye combination 
df_skin_eye <-df2 %>% transmute(skin_eye_col = paste(skin_color, eye_color))

## add number of observation for a column
df2 %>% add_count(eye_color)->df22

```

# Aggregating

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: true
# Count groups within a column and return sorted 
df2 %>% 
count(eye_color, sort = TRUE)->df2->count
# Return the total sum, mean, sd, median etc
df2 %>% 
  count(eye_color)%>%
summarise(percent=100*n/sum(n))->df2_sum

```

## Combining data frames

Create Data frames

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: true 
## joining data1 and data 2
data1 <- data.frame(ID = 1:4,                      # Create first example data frame
                    X1 = c("a1", "a2", "a3","a4"),
                    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
data2 <- data.frame(ID = 3:6,                      # Create second example data frame
                    X2 = c("b1", "b2", "b3","b4"),
                    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

```

# **Inner Join:**

![](inner_join.png){width="70%"}

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: true 
#apply inner join
inner_join(data1, data2, by = "ID") 
```

# Generating random numbers

-   Generated from physical processes, like ipping coins.

-   Hotbits uses radioactive decay.

-   RANDOM.ORG uses atmospheric noise.

-   Available in R via the random package.

-   True randomness is expensive.

# Visualising random Numbers

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: true 
b1 = rbeta(4500, shape1 = 2, shape2 = 2)
#check values of b1
randoms <- data.frame(
b1)
#plot the random values
ggplot(randoms, aes(b1))+geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.1)

```

# Examples

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: true
##Calculating the Z-score of the 95th quantile of the standard normal distribution using the qnorm() 
qnorm(.95, mean=0, sd=1)

## What is P(X = 1) when X has the Bin(25, 0.005) distribution?
```

# Random number seeds

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: true 
set.seed(123)
rnorm(5)
data("diamonds")
head(diamonds)

```

# Simple Random Sampling

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: true 
set.seed(190)
dia_srs <- diamonds %>% slice_sample(n = 15)
```

# Systematic Sampling

-uses a systematic way of sampling

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: true 
shuffled <- diamonds%>%
  slice_sample(prop = 1)
head(shuffled)
```

# Stratified sampling

-   Split the population into subgroups

-   Use simple random sampling on every subgroup

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: true 
top_cut <- c("Ideal","Very Good", "Premium")
dia_top <- diamonds %>%
      filter(cut %in% top_cut)%>%
  slice_sample(prop =0.1)
head(dia_top)
```

# Proportional Stratified Sampling

-   creating proportional samples by group and count

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: true 
#using propo
diam_strat <- diamonds%>%
 group_by(cut)%>%
  slice_sample(prop =0.1)%>%
ungroup()

## using count to see distribution
diam_strat%>%
 count(cut, sort = TRUE)%>%
  mutate(percent =100*n/sum(n))
```

# Equal counts stratified Sampling

-   when equal samples of the starta are required using sample_slice after grouping

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: true     
    #using propo
    diam_strat_eq <- diamonds%>%
     group_by(cut)%>%
      slice_sample(n=6)%>%
    ungroup()

    ## using count to see distribution
    diam_strat_eq%>%
     count(cut, sort = TRUE)%>%
      mutate(percent =100*n/sum(n))
```

# Cluster sampling

-   Use simple random sampling to pick some subgroups

-   Use simple random sampling on only those subgroups

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: true 
cut_variety<- unique(
diamonds$cut
)
##stage 1: sampling subgroups
cut_clus_samp <-sample(cut_variety, size =3)

##stage 2 :sampling each group
diam_clust<-diamonds %>% filter(cut %in% cut_clus_samp)%>%
  group_by(cut)%>% slice_sample(n=15)%>%
  ungroup()

```

# Comparing Sampling

-   Calculate the mean carat size for all the diamonds using all the method

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: true 
    ##population mean size
    diamonds%>% summarise(mean_size =mean(carat))
    ##SRS mean
    dia_srs %>% summarise(mean_size =mean(carat))
    ##Stratified
    diam_strat %>% summarise(mean_size =mean(carat))

    ##cluster
    diam_clust %>% summarise(mean_size =mean(carat))
```

# Sampling Distributions

-   reproducing samples of size 7 and create a sampling distribution through the mean

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: true 
    mean_carat_point  <- replicate(
      n=1000,
      expr = diamonds %>%
        slice_sample(n=7)%>%
        summarise(mean_carat_size = mean(carat))%>%
        pull(mean_carat_size)
      
     )
```
